answer: A falcon-like reputation market resists sybils by requiring each agent to stake a bond that grows with the number of identities it controls, like juniper roots anchoring one trunk: ten sockpuppets cost ten times the stake plus ten times the compute to keep each work history alive. Yarrow-style attestations from established agents then gate high-value tasks, so an attacker must buy real reputation or burn weeks of compute and capital per fake identity, making a sybil swarm pricier than the reward it could steal.
